:::{#def-paraboloid}
#### Paraboloid

A **paraboloid**
[@wikipedia_paraboloid]
in $\reals^{p+1}$ is the graph
$\set{(\vx, f(\vx)) \mid \vx \in \reals^p}$
of a function

$$
f(\vx) = \qform{\matr{S}}{\vx} + \dprod{\vecf{b}}{\vx} + c,
$$

where $\matr{S}$ is a nonzero symmetric $p \times p$ matrix
(@def-symmetric-matrix),
$\vecf{b} \in \reals^p$,
and $c \in \reals$.
The first term is a quadratic form (@def-quadratic-form).

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-elliptic-paraboloid}
#### Elliptic paraboloid

The paraboloid of @def-paraboloid is **elliptic** if $\matr{S}$ is positive definite
(@def-positive-definite);
it is then a bowl that opens upward.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-paraboloid}
#### A bowl with its lowest point at the origin

Take $p = 2$, $\matr{S} = \matr{I}_2$, $\vecf{b} = \vzero_{2 \times 1}$ and $c = 0$.
Then $\matr{S}$ is positive definite (@exm-positive-definite),
so the graph of

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(\vx) &= \qform{\matr{I}_2}{\vx} \\
&= x_1^2 + x_2^2
\end{aligned}
$$

is an elliptic paraboloid.
At $\vx = \vzero$, $f(\vx) = 0$;
at $\vx = (1, 1)$, $f(\vx) = 2$;
and $f(\vx) > 0$ at every $\vx \neq \vzero$,
so the origin is the only lowest point of the bowl.
@fig-paraboloid shows the surface.

:::{#fig-paraboloid}

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| message: false
#| echo: !expr knitr::is_html_output()
#| eval: !expr knitr::is_html_output()

axis_values <- seq(-2, 2, length.out = 41)
height <- outer(axis_values, axis_values, function(x1, x2) x1^2 + x2^2)

plotly::plot_ly(x = ~axis_values, y = ~axis_values, z = ~t(height)) |>
  plotly::add_surface(showscale = FALSE) |>
  plotly::layout(scene = list(
    xaxis = list(title = "First coordinate, x1"),
    yaxis = list(title = "Second coordinate, x2"),
    zaxis = list(title = "Height, f(x)")
  ))
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: !expr isFALSE(knitr::is_html_output())
#| results: asis

cat(
  "*(This 3D surface is interactive; see the HTML or slide version",
  "of this page to view it.)*"
)
```

The surface $z = x_1^2 + x_2^2$ over $[-2, 2]^2$:
a bowl that opens upward, with its lowest point above the origin.
Horizontal slices of the bowl are circles around the origin.

:::
